findings.reason: the single load-bearing fact of the section is the bound on the log, and its anchor currently points at unrelated code.
findings.text: §4 justifies its window design by citing the trim at `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` "near lines 2095–2100", but lines 2095–2100 are pointer-annotation and restore handling; the trim (`trim_service_log(..., limit=ADMISSION_VERDICT_LOG_MAX_BYTES, keep=ADMISSION_VERDICT_LOG_MAX_BYTES)`) is at `:2453–2454` and its bound at `:103`. A reader who checks the citation finds no trim and has to decide whether the 1 MiB bound is real before trusting the whole two-window design

findings.reason: without the copies' paths the "at zero" half of the after window is unmeasurable, and without their spacing the 4.5-hour coverage claim is unsupported, so a node could report a pass over a far shorter window than the plan asserts.
findings.text: the after-window hold counts are defined as "every retained copy of the live log taken after the admit service reloaded onto §2 and §3 (07:39–10:37Z and 20:46–22:12Z on 9 November, about 4.5 hours)", which names two time ranges and no path; the before window by contrast names a durable file (`~/.cache/reckon-claims/admission-verdicts-before-shared-default.jsonl`, present, 1,046,044 bytes, 212 rows). No retained 9 November copy is on a path the plan names, so the measuring node cannot reproduce or verify those counts. The coverage arithmetic compounds it: with the log bounded at ~80–90 minutes of tail, "about 4.5 hours" of coverage requires a copy roughly every 80 minutes across each range, and two snapshots would give at most ~3 hours, so the stated after-window size is only attainable if the copies' number and spacing are recorded

findings.reason: the assertion the section exists to prove can be satisfied by a window that measured nothing, which is the same defect the earlier review found in the ledger arm and which was answered there only for pairs.
findings.text: the done-when floors the ledger arm at five concurrent pairs but sets no floor on the retained-copy arm, which is what carries `held-on-claim verdicts on shared-root file paths at zero`; a copy holding a few quiet verdict rows yields zero by emptiness rather than by the fix, and the negative control it declares is on the *before* window, so it cannot catch a thin after-window copy

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the trim of `admission-verdicts.jsonl` is cited as `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` "near lines 2095–2100", but those lines are pointer-writeback exception handling; the trim call is at `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:2453` with the bound declared at `:103` (`ADMISSION_VERDICT_LOG_MAX_BYTES = 1_048_576`).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §4's done-when carries two arms and only the ledger arm has a volume floor; the retained-copy arm, which carries the "at zero" assertion, has none, so a thin copy window reads as a pass.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — the after-window hold counts are said to come from "every retained copy of the live log", named only by two time ranges and never by a path; I found no such copy under `~/.cache/reckon-claims/` (which holds only the 8 November before-window and an after-s32 copy) or in `docs/evidence/fragments/concurrent-edits-meet-at-the-merge/`, so a later reader and the measuring node alike have nothing to open.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §4 introduces no new symbol, and its one date-stamped clause ("amended on 9 November with the lead's approval") records plan provenance rather than leaking a stage label or ticket reference into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — all three checks hold. The stated root cause matches the cited evidence: the before-window snapshot parses to 212 pass records over exactly 2026-11-07T05:38:15Z–2026-11-08T12:33:24Z with 296 `held-on-claim` pointers, of which 283 name a path under a shared root (`reckon/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, `skills/`), so the exclusivity default really was holding shared-root paths. The declared mechanism produces the done-when: `docs/state/reckon/shared-write-paths.json` declares the four shared roots and the six exclusive patterns §2 names, and all 7,641 run-ledger records under `docs/state/reckon/runs/` carry `node_definition.write_paths` non-empty plus `dispatched_at` and `completed_at`, so the concurrent-pair arm is computable from the ledger as written. The real code path is named: the writer is the admission pass's verdict recorder in `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py`, and the live log confirms the bounded tail it describes (774 rows spanning 2026-11-09T21:19:56Z–22:50:23Z, about 90 minutes).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §4 declares one deliverable (one measurement, one evidence fragment) and every clause of the done-when serves that single measure.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` declares `s4: [s2, s3]` and `s5: [s2]`, every target resolves to a section that exists in the same plan, and §4's opening sentence ("once §2 and §3 are on main") matches the declaration; s2, s3 and s5 are declared done, so the queue's hold is the only entry §4 still needs.
